answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. It is effective because voting power is weighted by verifiable work over time, so a fresh flood of accounts cannot manufacture a decisive vote. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a knoll as the anchor of the cost.
